html:
Tassili n'Ajjer is a sandstone plateau in the Sahara of southeast Algeria with more than 15,000 rock paintings and engravings, made over thousands of years from about 10,000 BCE.

The images follow the history of the Sahara. The oldest show wild animals, such as elephants and hippos, from a wet, green time. Then come strange round-headed human figures, then herders with great herds of cattle, then horses and chariots, and last camels, as the desert spread.

The site became a World Heritage Site in 1982. With the Acacus across the border in Libya, it is the best evidence of how people lived in the Sahara before it dried. The Berber Tuareg still live in the area. See also Saharan herders.
sum: Tassili n'Ajjer is a sandstone plateau in the Sahara of southeast Algeria with more than 15,000 rock paintings and engravings, made over thousands of years from about 10,000 BCE.
